title: Ignition Failure
shortDescription: Water heater failed to light and has locked out.
fullDescription:
A.O. Smith power-vent and tankless heaters attempt multiple ignition trials. Error 001 indicates all trials failed. Causes: no gas, dirty flame rod, weak spark, or obstructed venting.

One reset is allowed. If it recurs, call a licensed technician.
safetyWarning: Do not reset repeatedly - gas can build up in the combustion chamber.

fixSteps.title: Confirm gas
fixSteps.instruction: Shutoff valve open, other gas appliances work.

fixSteps.title: Call technician
fixSteps.instruction: If recurs, pro cleans flame rod, checks igniter, gas pressure.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: How long should a flame rod last?

title: Flame Loss / Extinguish
fullDescription: The flame rod stopped sensing flame during firing. Common: dirty rod, gas pressure drop, or condensate flooding on power-vent units.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance - licensed repair recommended.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Tank or outlet temperature sensor open/short.
fullDescription: One of the tank/outlet thermistors is reporting an invalid value. Sensor replacement by a tech resolves.
safetyWarning: Power off before servicing sensors.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.a: Most units have tank + outlet sensors.

title: Burner Overheat
shortDescription: ECO (Energy Cut Off) tripped - burner over-temp.
fullDescription:
The high-limit / ECO device tripped due to excessive temperature at the burner or water jacket. Often caused by sediment buildup or a failed thermostat.

Many ECO trips are one-time manual reset devices that require tech replacement.
safetyWarning: Scald risk - water can be 180F+.
symptoms: Very hot water then no heat
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.a: Annually or more with hard water.

title: Condensate Trap Full / Blocked
shortDescription: Condensate drain blocked, water backing up.
fullDescription: Power-vent and condensing water heaters produce condensate. A plugged trap triggers safety shutdown to prevent flooding the combustion chamber.
safetyWarning: Flooded combustion chamber can damage the unit and create CO hazard.

fixSteps.title: Clear trap/drain
fixSteps.instruction: Flush trap per manual, verify drain flows.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Flow Switch Fault
shortDescription: Tankless flow switch not detecting flow or stuck.
fullDescription: On tankless models, the flow switch signals demand. If stuck or blocked with debris, the unit won't fire or misfires.
safetyWarning: Power off before servicing.

fixSteps.title: Increase flow
fixSteps.instruction: Open multiple hot taps to test minimum flow.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Check Vent / Air Intake
fullDescription: Power-vent heater cannot prove draft. Check vent terminations and intake for obstructions.
safetyWarning: Blocked vent = CO risk.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Check Flue / Blocked Exhaust
fullDescription: Flue gas temperature or pressure indicates blockage - debris, collapsed vent, or excessive condensate.
safetyWarning: Test CO detectors - immediate hazard possible.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Power Module Fault
shortDescription: Internal power supply / ignition module error.
fullDescription: The control's power supply or ignition module reports failure. Power cycle may clear; persistent fault needs board replacement.
safetyWarning: Do not open powered enclosure.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Fan / Blower Fault
fullDescription: Blower stalled or RPM feedback invalid. Usually bearings failing.
safetyWarning: CO risk - do not bypass.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Gas Valve Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Gas valve coil or wiring fault.
fullDescription: Electrical issue in gas valve circuit. Licensed gas technician required.
safetyWarning: Licensed repair only.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Anode/Water Chemistry Alert
shortDescription: Tank condition alert - smart models monitor anode.
fullDescription: Smart A.O. Smith heaters with condition monitoring may alert when anode is depleted or water conductivity is abnormal. Tank life is at risk without anode replacement.
safetyWarning: Prolonged operation with depleted anode leads to tank failure and leaks.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Inlet Water Too Cold / Freeze Risk
shortDescription: Inlet water temperature below operating range or freeze protection active.
fullDescription: On tankless units, very cold inlet water may exceed BTU capacity to meet setpoint, or freeze-protection circuit engaged. Relocate or insulate piping.
safetyWarning: Freeze damage voids warranty.

fixSteps.title: Insulate lines
fixSteps.instruction: Wrap supply lines with pipe insulation.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Outlet Temperature Too High
fullDescription: Outlet temperature above setpoint by a significant margin - possible scale buildup causing poor heat transfer then overshoot, or thermostat failure.
safetyWarning: Scald risk at 140F+ - limit outlet to 120F recommended.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Internal comm fault between control boards or display.
fullDescription: Multi-board systems lose communication. Power cycle first; persistent = harness or board issue.
safetyWarning: Don't open powered enclosure.
whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Inlet Thermistor Failure
shortDescription: Inlet temperature sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription:
AO Smith error 015 (commonly displayed as E15 on Vertex / Cyclone Xi) indicates the inlet thermistor circuit has detected an open or short. Without a valid inlet temperature, the controller cannot manage modulation safely and locks out.

Replace the thermistor or repair the harness; verify connector seating first.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the inlet thermistor connector at the control board.

whenToCallPro: Replacement requires draining the sensor port — recommend a technician unless you have the AO Smith service kit.

faq.a: No — the controller locks out to prevent unsafe operation.

title: Outlet Thermistor Failure
shortDescription: Outlet temperature sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription: Code 016 mirrors 015 but for the outlet thermistor. AO Smith uses the outlet sensor as the primary control feedback. A failed outlet thermistor will lock out the heater immediately.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the outlet thermistor connector.

whenToCallPro: Sensor replacement requires partial drain — call a technician for assistance.

faq.q: Can I swap inlet and outlet sensors?
faq.a: On most AO Smith models they are not interchangeable — verify with your manual.

title: Flue Temperature High
shortDescription: Flue temperature exceeded the high-limit threshold.
fullDescription: AO Smith error 017 indicates the flue thermistor has read above the safety limit, suggesting heat exchanger scaling, vent restriction, or burner mis-firing. The heater locks out to protect the heat exchanger and venting system.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
symptoms: Vent terminal warm to the touch

fixSteps.title: Inspect Vent
fixSteps.instruction: Check the vent terminal for obstruction.

whenToCallPro: Persistent 017 after descaling indicates a thermistor or vent installation issue — call a technician.

faq.a: Repeated trips can indicate venting problems — address promptly.

title: Inducer Fan Speed Error
shortDescription: Combustion inducer fan is not running at the commanded speed.
fullDescription: Code 018 on AO Smith reports the combustion fan tachometer is reporting unexpected RPM. Dirty blades, a worn motor bearing, or a PCB driver fault are typical.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum Fan Blades
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; remove cover and vacuum the fan blades.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not restore RPM, fan replacement is needed — call a technician.

faq.a: No — combustion safety requires the fan at correct speed.
Yes — but it is a service-level repair.

title: False Flame
shortDescription: Flame is detected when none is commanded.
fullDescription: AO Smith error 019 indicates the flame rod is reporting current when there should be none — typically due to moisture, a cracked insulator, or a stuck gas valve allowing residual combustion.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Drying Period
fixSteps.instruction: Power off for 1-2 hours in a heated space.

whenToCallPro: If drying and cleaning do not clear, the gas valve may be leaking — technician needed.

faq.a: Possibly — if the rod and ignition system are good, suspect a leaking gas valve.
If you smell gas, yes — and call your gas utility.

title: Outlet High-Limit Open
shortDescription: The mechanical outlet hi-limit thermal switch has opened.
fullDescription: Code 021 indicates the outlet hi-limit (mechanical thermal cutoff) has tripped. Causes are similar to thermistor-detected high-limit conditions: scaling, low flow, or a stuck mixing valve.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Cool and Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Allow 30 minutes cooldown, then power cycle.

whenToCallPro: If the code returns after descaling, the hi-limit switch needs replacement.

faq.a: Some models are auto-reset; others manual — check your model.
Scale impedes heat transfer and raises wall temperatures.

title: Communication Error – Display
shortDescription: Internal communication fault between the main control and display board.
fullDescription: Code 022 indicates the display board cannot communicate with the main control. Causes include a loose ribbon cable, a failed display, or main board fault.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
symptoms: Unit may operate but cannot be configured

fixSteps.title: Reseat Ribbon Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the display ribbon at both ends.

whenToCallPro: Persistent 022 after reseating cabling typically requires display or main board replacement.

faq.q: Can the unit operate without the display?
faq.a: Often, in default mode — but settings cannot be changed.

faq.q: Is this an electrical safety issue?

title: Anode Current Out of Range
shortDescription: Powered anode current is outside acceptable bounds.
fullDescription: On AO Smith powered-anode models (Vertex, hybrid), code 023 indicates the powered anode is drawing too little or too much current. Empty tank, insulation breakdown, or a failed anode are typical causes.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Verify Tank Full
fixSteps.instruction: Open a hot tap until water flows steadily; ensures tank is full.

whenToCallPro: Anode replacement is a moderately invasive task — call a plumber if not familiar.

faq.q: How often do anodes need replacement?
faq.a: Powered anodes typically last 20+ years; sacrificial anodes 3-5 years.
Short-term yes; long-term ignoring leads to tank corrosion.

title: Recirc Pump Fault
shortDescription: Internal recirculation pump did not start or is drawing abnormal current.
fullDescription: Code 024 on AO Smith units with internal recirculation indicates the pump is not responding. Causes include air-locked pump, dry-run, or motor failure.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
symptoms: No recirculation; cold sandwich at hot tap

fixSteps.title: Bleed Air
fixSteps.instruction: Bleed air from the recirc loop using the bleeder valve if equipped.

whenToCallPro: Pump replacement is a technician-level task involving partial drain.

faq.q: Will the heater work without recirc?
faq.a: Yes — but you lose instant hot water at the tap.

faq.q: How long does the pump last?

title: Outdoor Air Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor air temperature sensor (used on hybrid heat pump models) is out of range.
fullDescription: Code 025 on AO Smith hybrid heat pump water heaters indicates the outdoor (or ambient) air sensor is failed. The heat pump cannot decide between modes without it and may default to electric backup.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the ambient sensor connector.

whenToCallPro: Sensor replacement is straightforward but requires identifying the correct ambient sensor variant for your model.

faq.a: Yes — usually defaulting to electric backup mode.
Significantly — heat pump mode is 2-3x more efficient.

title: Stack Limit Tripped
fullDescription: AO Smith code 026 indicates the stack high-limit thermostat opened due to excessive flue temperature. Common causes are heat exchanger fouling and venting restriction.

fixSteps.title: Cool Down
fixSteps.instruction: Allow unit to fully cool before inspection.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Vent
fixSteps.instruction: Check for restrictions, ice, or nesting.

whenToCallPro: If vent and descale do not resolve 026, call a technician for combustion analysis.

title: Inlet Thermistor Open
shortDescription: Cold inlet thermistor circuit is open.
fullDescription: Code 027 means the inlet thermistor circuit shows an open. The unit cannot calculate firing rate and locks out.
whenToCallPro: If sensor measures correct, the PCB is at fault — call a technician.

title: Inlet Thermistor Short
shortDescription: Cold inlet thermistor circuit is shorted.
fullDescription: Code 028 is the short-circuit counterpart to 027. Pinched wires or water in the connector are the typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open and dry the thermistor connector.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Resistance check; near zero indicates short.

whenToCallPro: Persistent short after replacement is a wiring or PCB issue — call a technician.

title: Outlet Thermistor Open
shortDescription: Hot outlet thermistor circuit is open.
fullDescription: Code 029 indicates the outlet thermistor reads open. The unit will not fire because outlet temperature protection is unavailable.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Plug
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, reseat outlet thermistor connector.

whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good but 029 remains, call a technician.

title: Outlet Thermistor Short
fullDescription: Code 030 indicates a short in the outlet thermistor circuit.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short after replacement indicates wiring damage — call a technician.

title: Vent Pressure Fault
shortDescription: Vent pressure switch fault during operation.
fullDescription: Code 031 means the vent pressure switch changed state unexpectedly during the run cycle, suggesting venting restriction, tubing condensate, or switch failure.

fixSteps.title: Drain Tubing
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and clear pressure switch tubing.

whenToCallPro: If venting is clean and switch is good, call a technician for combustion check.

title: Recirculation Pump Fault
shortDescription: Internal or external recirc pump not responding.
fullDescription: Code 032 indicates a problem with the recirc pump — open winding, seized impeller, or relay failure on the PCB.

fixSteps.title: Test Pump
fixSteps.instruction: With unit off, try to spin pump shaft.

whenToCallPro: Pump replacement on AO Smith units typically requires a plumber.

title: Internal Communication Error
fullDescription: Code 033 means the display and main control are not communicating. A reseated ribbon cable resolves many cases; otherwise the display or PCB needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat ribbon between display and PCB.

whenToCallPro: If reseating fails, the display or PCB needs replacement — call a technician.

title: Maintenance Reminder
fullDescription: Code 034 is a service reminder. The unit continues to operate; perform descale, filter cleaning, and venting check, then reset the counter.

fixSteps.title: Reset Counter
fixSteps.instruction: Reset from service menu after work.

whenToCallPro: If preferred, call a plumber for annual service.

title: Air Filter Service
shortDescription: Inlet air filter is dirty and reducing combustion air.
fullDescription: Code 035 indicates the air intake filter (on direct-vent models) needs cleaning. Reduced combustion air leads to inefficient operation and may eventually trigger combustion faults.

fixSteps.title: Locate Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Filter is at the air intake fitting.

fixSteps.title: Reset Counter
fixSteps.instruction: Reset air filter timer in menu.

whenToCallPro: If 035 returns immediately, the sensor may be at fault — call a technician.

safetyWarning: Gas appliance — turn off gas supply and disconnect power before servicing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor/flow
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor wiring and water flow.

title: Anode Rod Service Required
fullDescription: Code 046 on AO Smith Vertex and Voltex models with powered anodes indicates the anode controller is requesting service. The unit can keep operating but tank corrosion protection is reduced.

fixSteps.title: Schedule Service
fixSteps.instruction: Call a plumber to inspect and replace the powered anode.

whenToCallPro: Powered anode replacement is a pro job.

title: Mixing Valve Calibration Required
fullDescription: Code 047 on AO Smith units with motorized anti-scald mixing valves indicates the calibration timer expired or the position feedback drifted.
safetyWarning: Scald risk if calibration is wrong.

fixSteps.title: Run Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Use the service menu calibration routine.

whenToCallPro: Service menu access typically requires installer code.

faq.a: Wear in actuator gears can introduce small errors.

title: Vacation Mode Active
fullDescription: Code 048 is informational - the unit is in vacation mode and maintaining a low setpoint to save energy.

fixSteps.title: Exit Vacation Mode
fixSteps.instruction: Press the vacation button on the controller.

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.q: How long until I have hot water again?

title: Heat Pump Defrost Active
shortDescription: Heat pump unit running defrost cycle.
fullDescription: Code 049 on AO Smith Voltex hybrid units indicates the heat pump is currently in a defrost cycle. Backup electric elements may run during this period.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Allow defrost cycle to complete (5-15 min).

whenToCallPro: Not needed.

faq.a: Yes, especially in cool ambient conditions.

title: Compressor Overcurrent
fullDescription: Code 050 on Voltex hybrid units indicates the heat pump compressor drew current above its safe limit. The unit will switch to electric backup.
safetyWarning: High current may indicate failing compressor - do not bypass safeties.
symptoms: Heat pump not running, hot water still works on elements
whenToCallPro: Always call a pro for compressor faults.

faq.q: Will I still have hot water?
faq.a: Yes - the electric elements maintain temperature.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Evaporator coil sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: Code 051 indicates the evaporator coil temperature sensor is reading out of range. The heat pump will run inefficiently or shut down.

fixSteps.title: Re-seat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open the access panel and re-seat the evap sensor.

whenToCallPro: Replacement requires accessing the heat pump module.

faq.a: Yes, on electric elements only - reduced efficiency.

title: Discharge Temperature High
shortDescription: Heat pump discharge line temperature exceeded limit.
fullDescription: Code 052 occurs when the compressor discharge line temperature exceeds its safe limit, often due to low refrigerant or poor airflow.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA certification.

fixSteps.title: Clean Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the heat pump air filter.

fixSteps.title: Verify Clearances
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure 1000 cu ft of space and unobstructed return air.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant work requires a pro.

faq.q: Where should the unit be located?
faq.a: In a space with at least 1000 cu ft and 50-120F.

title: Suction Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Heat pump suction line sensor fault.
fullDescription: Code 053 indicates the suction line temperature sensor is out of range.
whenToCallPro: Replacement requires opening the heat pump module.

faq.a: May fall back to electric elements only.

title: Heat Pump Communication Lost
shortDescription: Main controller lost communication with heat pump module.
fullDescription: Code 054 indicates the main controller cannot communicate with the heat pump board, often due to a loose ribbon cable.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power before opening covers.

fixSteps.title: Re-seat Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Re-seat the ribbon cable between controller and heat pump board.

whenToCallPro: Board replacement requires a pro.

faq.a: Vibration or aging connectors can loosen the ribbon cable.

title: Condensate Pan Full
shortDescription: Heat pump condensate pan float switch tripped.
fullDescription: Code 055 indicates the condensate drain pan float switch detected high water level. The heat pump will shut down to prevent overflow.
safetyWarning: Standing water near electrical components - turn off power before service.

fixSteps.title: Clear Drain
fixSteps.instruction: Clear the condensate drain line of any blockage.

whenToCallPro: If float switch stuck, hire a pro.

faq.q: Why does the heat pump make condensate?
faq.a: It dehumidifies the surrounding air, producing condensate water.
